title: Quantum query-to-communication lifting
formal: Do there exist constants \(C\ge1\) and an integer \(k\ge0\) such that, for every \(n\ge2\), there is a total nonconstant Boolean communication gadget \(g_n:\{0,1\}^{a_n}\times\{0,1\}^{b_n}\to\{0,1\}\), with finite positive integers \(a_n,b_n\), for which every partial Boolean function \(f:D\to\{0,1\}\), \(D\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), satisfies \[\frac{Q_{1/3}(f)}{C(\log_2n)^k}\ \le\ Q^*_{1/3}(f\circ g_n^n)\ \le\ C(\log_2n)^k Q_{1/3}(f)?\] Here \(Q_{1/3}\) is quantum query complexity and \(Q^*_{1/3}\) is two-party quantum communication complexity with unrestricted prior entanglement. Both have worst-case error at most \(1/3\). The gadget depends on \(n\), but not on \(D\) or \(f\), and the constants are common to the entire family.
why: Quantum query complexity captures information obtainable from an oracle, while communication complexity measures information exchanged between separated parties. A universal lifting theorem would tightly connect these two models across all Boolean promise problems. The demand for only polylogarithmic loss is substantially stronger than transferring a weaker lower-bound measure or obtaining an arbitrary polynomial relation.
status_note: The original question remains explicitly open in the checked ICALP 2026 primary discussion. The CCC 2021 and ICALP 2026 positive results have weaker lower-bound measures, additional hypotheses or model restrictions. Bounded checks through 2026-09-16 did not verify a full resolution; this is not an exhaustive survey of all subsequent work.

progress.text: Ben-David and Kothari state the missing bounded-error and zero-error lifting questions in Section 7.1; Theorem 18 gives an implication from a hypothetical zero-error lifting theorem to bounded-error lifting.
Ben-David’s CS 860 notes state Conjecture 8.6 with an input-length-dependent gadget of polylogarithmic communication cost.
Anshu, Ben-David and Kundu give bounded-round and conditional adversary lifting results, retaining the distinction from full quantum lifting.
Wu, Yang and Yao establish a hybrid classical-quantum lifting theorem at ICALP 2026 and still identify unrestricted quantum query-to-communication lifting as open.

importance.reason: A general quantum lifting theorem would transfer the full strength of quantum query lower bounds to two-party communication, including arbitrary promise problems. The gap persists despite powerful classical lifting theorems and partial quantum analogues, making it a central structural question about quantum information complexity.
importance.basis: Individual reading of the TQC 2019 question, Ben-David’s explicit lifting conjecture, CCC 2021 adversary results and the ICALP 2026 primary discussion of the unresolved general theorem.

sentences: A lifting theorem would turn the quantum query complexity of a Boolean promise problem into the communication complexity of a composed two-party problem.
The question asks for one gadget per input length that works for every partial outer function.
Both complexity measures should agree up to common polylogarithmic factors.
The communication model allows arbitrary prior entanglement and an unrestricted number of rounds.
Known bounded-round, adversary and hybrid lifting results leave this general bounded-error transfer open in the checked 2026 source.

definitions: For \(z\in D\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), a query applies \(O_z:|i,b,w\rangle\mapsto|i,b\mathbin{\oplus}z_i,w\rangle\), where \(i\in[n]\), \(b\in\{0,1\}\), and \(w\) denotes an arbitrary finite workspace. A quantum query algorithm starts in an input-independent state, uses arbitrary input-independent local quantum operations and measurements between queries, and produces \(f(z)\) with probability at least \(2/3\) on every promised \(z\). \(Q_{1/3}(f)\) is the minimum worst-case number of calls to \(O_z\), counting all branches. Computation between queries is free; there is no uniformity or finite-gate-set restriction. A function constant on its promise, including an empty promise, has query complexity zero. For the composed communication problem Alice receives \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\) with \(x_i\in\{0,1\}^{a_n}\), Bob receives \(y=(y_1,\ldots,y_n)\) with \(y_i\in\{0,1\}^{b_n}\), and the promise is that \(z=(g_n(x_i,y_i))_{i=1}^n\) belongs to \(D\). Bob must output \(f(z)\). A protocol has arbitrary finite-dimensional local registers and any finite-dimensional shared initial state independent of the inputs, with no bound on its entanglement. It may exchange messages in both directions, perform arbitrary local quantum operations and measurements depending on its own input and local history, and use shared or private randomness. All communicated qubits in both directions count; a classical bit sent as a message costs one qubit. Local computation, local memory, and the shared initial state are free. \(Q^*_{1/3}\) is the minimum worst-case total communication over protocols whose error probability is at most \(1/3\) for every promised input pair. The number of rounds is unrestricted, subject to finite protocol length; communication cost includes every branch. Query algorithms and protocols may depend on the particular finite function and promise and need not be uniformly constructible. The gadget family is existential: no efficient method to print its truth table, input-length bound on \(a_n,b_n\), or fixed gadget independent of \(n\) is required. Its communication cost is nevertheless constrained by the universal two-sided inequality, which includes coordinate functions \(f(z)=z_i\). All logarithms in the inequality are base two.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean proof of the existence of this gadget family and common constants with both inequalities for all \(n,D,f\), or a complete Lean proof that no such family and constants exist. A theorem for a restricted class of outer functions, a fixed round bound, approximate polynomial degree instead of quantum query complexity, or a polynomial rather than polylogarithmic loss does not meet the stated affirmative target. The target is bounded-error lifting; a separate zero-error theorem is not also required.

context_blocks.text: The source asks about both bounded-error and zero-error quantum lifting. This card selects its bounded-error branch, retaining partial outer functions and polylogarithmic losses. The source’s reductions between lifting statements are conditional implications, not a proof of the missing lifting theorem.

Ben-David’s lecture notes state a gadget-family conjecture in which the gadget may depend on the outer input length and has only polylogarithmic communication cost. This card does not add a constant-size, logarithmic-input-length or efficient-construction requirement.

The communication convention is made explicit as the entanglement-assisted model used in the later quantum lifting literature. This is a documented choice within the original general question, whose short extraction did not specify the shared-state convention. The quantification over partial functions follows the original paper’s Section 7.

The CCC 2021 work proves an unconditional bounded-round lifting result for a classical adversary measure and a conditional result for a simplified positive-weight quantum adversary bound. Neither is a general, unconditional lifting theorem for full quantum query complexity with unrestricted rounds.

The ICALP 2026 hybrid theorem lifts approximate degree within a model that begins with classical communication and then uses quantum messages. Its Introduction explicitly retains general quantum query-to-communication lifting as a major open problem. Approximate degree and full quantum query complexity are distinct targets.
